title: Mary and the saints
hookLine: a daily Marian prayer and a saint for the year
tomorrow: what happens to a rule when life breaks your routine?

cards: The first day somewhere new: a cafeteria, a locker room, an office, eyes scanning for one familiar face. Who walks in with you? John's Gospel tells of a moment at the cross.
Jesus sees his mother, and the disciple he loves standing beside her, and gives them to each other. To her: "Woman, behold thy son." To him: "Behold thy mother."

teach.b: John adds: "And from that hour, the disciple took her to his own." Catholics hear that as a gift to every disciple, a mother for the road.
So a rule for life often keeps one short daily prayer to Mary, short enough never to skip: a Hail Mary in the car, the Angelus at noon, a decade before sleep. Then the saints.
The letter to the Hebrews says believers have "so great a cloud of witnesses over our head," people who ran this race before and now surround the ones still running.
Catholics honor them and ask their prayers; worship belongs to God alone.
One to tell a friend: some Catholic families keep a custom of drawing a saint's name at the new year, and letting that saint, not the one they'd have picked, keep them company all year.
A stranger who becomes a friend. Now the week comes back: six pieces of a rule, in a round.

how: Many Catholics pray a short daily prayer to Mary, such as the Hail Mary, the Angelus or a decade of the rosary; some families draw a patron saint's name at the new year to learn about and pray with through the year.

games.q: your friend drew Saint Jerome from the bowl at new year and groans: 'i wanted someone fun.' what fits the custom?
o: draw again until a saint you already like comes up.
keep him. the saint you didn't pick becomes a friend you get to know.
skip the saints and pray only to Mary; that covers it.
games.why: the custom is company you didn't choose: a year with someone from the cloud of witnesses, who stops being a stranger.

practice: If you pray, say one Hail Mary out loud, slowly, as if someone were listening beside you. If you don't, say aloud the name of one saint or one person of faith whose story you'd like to know better this year.
Let that name sit with you while the time runs.

wordCard.voice: Mary and the saints. A mother given from the cross, and a cloud of witnesses who ran the road first.

orig.note: Greek: a cloud of witnesses, in the letter to the Hebrews.

carryVoice: The line to keep: company for the road, a mother and a saint who walk in with you. See you next week.
